query: Consider the following context: Refractory high-entropy alloys (HEAs) are promising candidates for next-generation nuclear applications, particularly fusion reactors, due to their excellent high-temperature mechanical properties and irradiation resistance. In that context, which material can be used for low-activation structural material for high-temperature plasma-facing components (PFCs) in fusion reactors, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Selecting specific alloying elements in refractory high-entropy alloys (HEAs) will reduce activation levels while maintaining high-temperature stability, making them suitable for low-activation structural materials in high-temperature plasma-facing components (PFCs) in fusion reactors.
generation.material_initial_state: Refractory high-entropy alloys (HEAs) with standard alloying elements.
generation.intervention: Modification of the alloying elements in HEAs to include low-activation materials.
generation.conditions: High-temperature environments typical of fusion reactors.
generation.structural_mediator: The composition of the HEA, particularly the choice of alloying elements.
generation.mechanism: The selection of alloying elements influences both the activation properties and the mechanical stability of the material under high-temperature conditions.
generation.predicted_outcome: A decrease in activation levels while retaining or enhancing mechanical stability at high temperatures.
generation.baseline: Standard refractory HEAs with conventional alloying elements that may have higher activation levels.
generation.boundary: The hypothesis is limited to the context of high-temperature plasma-facing components in fusion reactors.
generation.uncertainty: The exact effects of specific alloying element changes on activation levels and mechanical properties are not fully known.

falsification_experiment.design: Conduct a comparative study of HEAs with different alloying element compositions under simulated fusion reactor conditions.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the modified HEAs show higher activation levels or significantly reduced mechanical stability compared to the baseline, the hypothesis is falsified.
